title: What if the sun never set again?
formula: Strange act (29 days awake, your toaster tells you to relax) -> why (the sun stopped 29 days ago) -> fun first (kids skip bedtime, dad mows 11 times) -> the rule (no dark, no sleep) -> darkness economy world tour ($900 closets, theater hotels, the fridge guy) -> rival's perfect version (Kyle paints his basement black, sells night at $500 an hour) + mocker ('Hey Sunshine!') -> weird prep, mystery kept (a hole in a cereal box, a dot on the window every morning, your mattress in the middle of the street, an alarm for 2:14 PM) -> running bit (even the toaster thinks you snapped) -> setback (the town cooks, Kyle's line round the block, mom trades him the car) -> tension stretch (2:14, nothing happens, Kyle laughs) -> payoff mid-danger (a bite out of the sun in the box; 'You see,' the Moon never stopped; the dots were the Moon; little brother in front of the TV) -> peak (dim, cooler, streetlights on, the last sliver goes, stars) -> reversal: the rival's product goes free (the town pours out of his basement; 'That's MY night!') -> nobody hears him, the street is asleep -> loop: you finally listen to the toaster.
loop: Line 1: 'You haven't slept in 29 days, and your toaster just told you to relax.' Last: 'Three minutes of night. And for once, you listen to the toaster.'

voiceNotes.kyle: Liam (ElevenLabs premade): energetic young man, a loud hustler neighbour selling darkness

facts: Scenario premise: the sun stops in the sky (never explained; a real stop of Earth's spin would be far worse, so the script claims no cause). The Moon keeps orbiting, so it still crosses the frozen sun.
The Moon laps the sun about every 29.5 days (the synodic month), moving roughly 12 degrees a day across the sky; it is often visible in daylight, so you can track it with dots on a window.

A total solar eclipse needs the Moon at a node of its orbit, so a dead-centre one on this pass is luck (played as the payoff). With Earth not spinning, the Moon's shadow crosses the ground faster than usual, so totality would be short: ~3 minutes is plausible (real totality runs up to ~7.5 min).

During totality the sky goes dark enough for stars and planets, air temperature drops by up to ~10 F, light-sensor streetlights switch on, and birds and insects act like it is night (NASA eclipse pages).
A pinhole in a box projects the sun's image, so you see the 'bite' safely (NASA / AAS eclipse safety).
Melatonin, the sleepy hormone, is released in darkness and suppressed by light; after a few days without sleep people start to hallucinate (sleep-deprivation studies).
Without nights the surface never gets its nightly cooling, so heat keeps building (radiative balance); asphalt softens in extreme heat.

Comic exaggeration: the talking toaster (a hallucination), dad mowing 11 times, $900 closets, theater hotels, the man sleeping in his fridge, Kyle's $500-an-hour basement, mom trading the car, the whole street falling asleep in 3 minutes.

lines.narration: You haven't slept in 29 days, and your toaster just told you to *relax*.
lines.spoken: You haven't slept in twenty-nine days, and your toaster just told you to relax.
lines.scene: Cold open, your kitchen: you at the counter, eyes red and twitching, hair wild; the toaster has a face (two dials for eyes, the slot a mouth) and mouths 'relax' as two slices pop up. Behind you the window blazes with noon sun, and the microwave clock reads 3:00 AM. Hard cut on '29' out the window: the sun, huge and glaring over the rooftops.
lines.camera: MCU on you and the toaster, the microwave clock sharp; hard cut up to the sun on '29', back to the toaster on 'relax'
lines.gag: The toaster talks, the toast pops on 'relax'

lines.narration: Because 29 days ago, the sun stopped in the sky... and never *set* again.
lines.spoken: Because twenty-nine days ago, the sun stopped in the sky... and never set again.
lines.scene: The sun sliding down toward the horizon over the town, then halting dead with a jolt and a little bounce; on the street below, every shadow freezes. A sundial in a garden with its shadow stuck.
lines.camera: Wide on the sky, a snap shake on the stop, hard cut to the frozen sundial
lines.gag: The sun brakes like a car, and bounces

lines.narration: At first, it's *awesome*. Kids skip bedtime. Your dad mows the lawn *eleven* times.
lines.spoken: At first, it's AWESOME. Kids skip bedtime. Your dad mows the lawn eleven times.
lines.scene: Your street in full sun: kids on bikes doing wheelies past a 'BEDTIME?' sign kicked over; your dad in a sun hat mowing stripes into an already bald lawn, a tally of 11 chalked on the fence.
lines.camera: Fast tracking move along the street, MS on Dad on 'eleven'
lines.gag: The lawn is mowed down to dirt

lines.narration: But your brain only makes its sleepy juice in the *dark*.
lines.scene: Full-frame x-ray insert of your head: a little tap inside your brain dripping blue sleepy drops; a beam of sunlight hits it and the tap screws itself shut.
lines.camera: Hard cut to the insert, push-in on the tap
lines.gag: Sunlight slams the brain's sleep tap shut

lines.narration: So nobody sleeps, and darkness becomes the most expensive thing on *Earth*.
lines.scene: A shop window on your street with a velvet display stand holding a small black box under a spotlight, price tag $10,000; a crowd of red-eyed people pressed against the glass.
lines.camera: Push-in on the black box past the crowd's heads
lines.gag: A box of 'darkness' displayed like a diamond

lines.narration: A closet rents for $900 a night. Movie theaters turn into *hotels*.
lines.spoken: A closet rents for nine hundred dollars a night. Movie theaters turn into hotels.
lines.scene: Two beats: a closet door with a 'FOR RENT $900' sign and a man curled up inside among the coats; a cinema with rows of people asleep in the seats under a 'HOTEL' banner over the marquee.
lines.camera: Hard cut per beat, the HOTEL banner on 'hotels'
lines.gag: A man curled up asleep among the coats in a rented closet

lines.narration: And a guy in Ohio sleeps in his *fridge*.
lines.spoken: And a guy in Ohio sleeps in his FRIDGE.
lines.scene: A man folded inside his fridge next to the milk, hugging a pillow; the door swings shut and the light clicks off.
lines.camera: MS on the open fridge, the door shuts on 'fridge'
lines.gag: The fridge light clicks off and he smiles

lines.narration: Your neighbor Kyle paints his basement black, and sells night for $500 an *hour*.
lines.spoken: Your neighbor Kyle paints his basement black, and sells night for five hundred dollars an hour.
lines.scene: Kyle in shades and a gold chain at his basement steps beside a neon sign 'KYLE'S NIGHT CLUB - $500/HR' and a price board, a line of sleepy neighbours in pajamas holding cash and pillows.
lines.camera: Low angle MS on Kyle, rack to the price board on 'hour'
lines.gag: A line of people in pajamas holding cash and pillows

lines.narration: "Hey, Sunshine! Want some night? Cash *only*!"
lines.speaker: kyle
lines.scene: Kyle leaning over his fence toward you, fanning a stack of cash, grinning; the line behind him laughs.
lines.camera: Telephoto MCU of Kyle, the line blurred behind
lines.gag: Kyle fans himself with cash

lines.narration: You can't afford it. So you get *weird*.
lines.scene: Your empty wallet: a moth flies out. You narrow your eyes, scheming.
lines.camera: Insert on the wallet, hard cut to your scheming face
lines.gag: A moth flies out of your wallet

lines.narration: You poke a tiny hole in a cereal *box*.
lines.scene: Macro: your finger pushes a pencil through the side of a cereal box; you peer into the box with one eye.
lines.camera: Macro on the pencil going through on 'box'
lines.gag: You wear the cereal box on your head

lines.narration: Every morning, or what your phone calls morning, you draw one dot on your *window*.
lines.scene: Your bedroom window with a black marker in your hand: a row of dots arcs across the glass toward the blazing sun; you add one more. Your phone on the sill says 7:00 AM under the same noon sun.
lines.camera: MCU through the glass, the new dot lands on 'window'
lines.gag: A dotted trail creeping toward the sun

lines.narration: You drag your mattress into the middle of the *street*, and set an alarm for 2:14 PM.
lines.spoken: You drag your mattress into the middle of the street, and set an alarm for two-fourteen P.M.
lines.scene: You hauling your mattress down the driveway, leaning into it, and dropping it in the middle of the hot road; then your phone alarm screen: 2:14 PM.
lines.camera: Tracking side-on with the mattress drag, insert on the alarm
lines.gag: A bed in the middle of the road

lines.narration: Kyle thinks you've finally *snapped*. Honestly? So does the *toaster*.
lines.spoken: Kyle thinks you've finally snapped. Honestly? So does the toaster.
lines.scene: Kyle laughing at you on your mattress in the road; cut to the toaster on your kitchen counter, its dial eyes rolling.
lines.camera: MS two-shot over the fence, hard cut to the toaster on 'toaster'
lines.gag: The toaster rolls its eyes

lines.narration: And with no night to cool off, your town cooks like a pan left on the *stove*.
lines.scene: The porch thermometer needle creeping past 110; a sneaker peeling up off the soft asphalt with a long sticky string; heat shimmer over the street, the lawn yellow.
lines.camera: Macro on the needle, low macro on the sneaker on 'stove'
lines.gag: The road stretches like gum under a shoe

lines.narration: Kyle's line wraps around the block. Your mom trades him the *car*.
lines.scene: A wide of the line snaking down the street to Kyle's basement; your mom handing Kyle the car keys, Kyle pocketing them with a wink.
lines.camera: Crane up over the line, hard cut to the keys on 'car'
lines.gag: Kyle spins your mom's car keys on his finger

lines.narration: Then, 2:14 PM. Your alarm *rings*.
lines.spoken: Then, two-fourteen P.M. Your alarm rings.
lines.scene: You on your mattress in the road, the phone buzzing and jumping in your hand.
lines.camera: MCU on you, the phone jumps on 'rings'
lines.gag: The phone buzzes off the mattress

lines.narration: You look up, and nothing happens. Ten seconds. Still *nothing*.
lines.spoken: You look up, and nothing happens. Ten seconds. Still... nothing.
lines.scene: You staring up at the blank blazing sky; sweat drop on your face; the street watching you from the line.
lines.camera: Low angle on your face, push-in, the sweat drop on 'nothing'
lines.gag: The whole line turns to stare at you

lines.narration: "Nice alarm, *Sunshine*!"
lines.speaker: kyle
lines.scene: Kyle at the top of his basement steps, laughing, pointing at you with your mom's car keys.
lines.camera: Telephoto MCU of Kyle
lines.gag: Kyle points at you with your mom's car keys

lines.narration: Then you look in your cereal box, and the sun has a *bite* missing.
lines.scene: Inside the cereal box: the pinhole projects a little bright disc on the white cardboard, and a dark round bite is eating into its edge.
lines.camera: POV into the box, the bite slides in on 'bite'
lines.gag: The sun looks like a cookie with a bite out of it

lines.narration: You see, the sun stopped. But the Moon *didn't*.
lines.spoken: You see, the sun stopped. But the Moon DIDN'T.
lines.scene: Up in the sky, the dark disc of the Moon sliding onto the blazing sun.
lines.camera: Telephoto on the sun, the Moon slides in on 'didn't'
lines.gag: The Moon strolls in front of the sun

lines.narration: Those dots on your window? That was the Moon, sneaking closer every *day*.
lines.scene: Your window: the dotted trail on the glass lines up exactly with the Moon now touching the sun, the last dot right on it.
lines.camera: Match cut from the window dots to the sky on 'day'
lines.gag: The dot trail ends exactly on the Moon

lines.narration: Every 29 days, it walks in front of the sun, like your little brother in front of the *TV*.
lines.spoken: Every twenty-nine days, it walks in front of the sun, like your little brother in front of the TV.
lines.scene: Mini-set: a living room, a family on the couch, a little brother strolls in front of the bright TV and the room goes dark.
lines.camera: Dissolve to the TV mini-set, the room darkens on 'TV'
lines.gag: The little brother blocks the TV and the whole family groans

lines.narration: The street goes *dim*. The air drops ten degrees. The streetlights flick *on*.
lines.scene: The whole street dimming to deep blue, a breeze through the trees, people in the line shivering happily; one by one the streetlights blink on down the road.
lines.camera: Wide down the street, the lights click on toward the lens on 'on'
lines.gag: The streetlights wake up confused

lines.narration: Then the last sliver of sun *vanishes*.
lines.scene: Telephoto on the sun: the last bright bead winks out and the corona blooms around a black disc.
lines.camera: Telephoto hold, the bead vanishes on 'vanishes'
lines.gag: A black sun with a white crown

lines.narration: And for the first time in 29 days... the *stars* come out.
lines.spoken: And for the first time in twenty-nine days... the stars come out.
lines.scene: Deep night over your street: stars filling the sky above the black sun, an owl hooting on a wire, crickets, fireflies blinking over the yellow lawns.
lines.camera: Slow crane up from you on the mattress to the starry sky
lines.gag: An owl on the wire hoots like it's been waiting a month

lines.narration: Kyle's whole basement empties into the street, to look *up*.
lines.scene: Kyle's customers pouring up out of his basement in pajamas, dropping their cash, staring up at the stars, mouths open.
lines.camera: Low wide on the basement steps, the crowd floods past the lens
lines.gag: Cash falls out of their pockets as they look up

lines.narration: "Hey! That's MY *night*!"
lines.speaker: kyle
lines.scene: Kyle alone at the top of his steps under the stars, shaking his fist at the sky, his neon sign flickering.
lines.camera: MCU on Kyle, his sign flickers behind him
lines.gag: Kyle shakes his fist at the Moon

lines.narration: Nobody hears him. The whole street is already *asleep*.
lines.scene: Wide of the street under the stars: neighbours asleep on the lawns, on the hoods of cars, in the road beside your mattress; your dad asleep on the mower.
lines.camera: Slow overhead crane across the sleeping street
lines.gag: Dad asleep on the lawnmower

lines.narration: Three minutes of night. And for once, you listen to the *toaster*.
lines.spoken: Three minutes of night. [sighs] And for once, you listen to the toaster.
lines.scene: Close-up of you on your mattress in the road, starlight on your face, eyes closing into a happy smile; through your kitchen window behind you, the toaster gives a little smile too.
lines.camera: Mirror of the cold open: MCU on you with the toaster in frame behind, slow push-in, eyes shut on 'toaster'
lines.gag: The toaster smiles, satisfied
